name: Tycoons, Trusts and Trademarks
description: The founders who built great fortunes and brands, and the companies they made, from the railway barons and Rockefeller's oil trust to Ford, Sony, Microsoft and Amazon.

checkpoints.name: Railways and steel
checkpoints.note: Cornelius Vanderbilt moves from steamboats into railways, Andrew Carnegie rises from telegraph boy to railway manager and then turns to steel, and in 1870 John D. Rockefeller founds Standard Oil in Cleveland.

checkpoints.name: Trusts and trademarks
checkpoints.note: Rockefeller's oil trust, Carnegie's steel and J. P. Morgan's banking dominate America until the courts break up Standard Oil in 1911. George Eastman's Kodak, Coca-Cola and Madam C. J. Walker's hair products show how a trusted brand can build a fortune, and Henry Ford starts his motor company in 1903.

checkpoints.name: Cars, couture and cartoons
checkpoints.note: Henry Ford's moving assembly line puts ordinary families in cars. Coco Chanel builds a fashion house, Walt Disney a cartoon studio that grows into a media company, and Konosuke Matsushita an electrical firm from a small Osaka workshop.

checkpoints.name: The mass market
checkpoints.note: Akio Morita's Sony and Soichiro Honda's motorcycles carry Japanese brands around the world, Sam Walton opens the first Walmart in 1962, and Ingvar Kamprad sells flat-pack furniture to millions.

checkpoints.name: Digital fortunes
checkpoints.note: Bill Gates's Microsoft and Steve Jobs's Apple build fortunes on software and personal computers, Anita Roddick builds a cosmetics chain, and Warren Buffett grows rich by patient investing. Jeff Bezos's Amazon, Jack Ma's online market, Mark Zuckerberg's Facebook, now Meta, and Elon Musk's car and rocket firms follow.
